disposition_records.T20-CI-TOOLCHAIN-TYPECHECK: PR #56 CI run 1: Swift 6.0 (Xcode 16.2) and 6.2 (Xcode 26.3) reported 'unable to type-check this expression in reasonable time' at Benchmarks/VectorCoreBench/Formatters/CSVWriter.swift:71 (every build job; introduced by d2d579a) and Tests/ComprehensiveTests/BatchConfigurationContractTests.swift:397 (Xcode 16.2 Release). Both expressions are now built from typed parts with the same element expressions, order and Double operations. Swift 6.4 accepted both originals, and its -warn-long-expression-type-checking=100 scan flagged neither; the four slowest expressions it did flag (237-468 ms) are from main, where CI passes. So the local compiler cannot predict this class, and CI's toolchain matrix is its closure.

disposition_records.T20-R2-TYPECHECK-FIXTURES: PR #56 CI run 2 compiled the test targets on CI's toolchains for the first time. Swift 6.0 and 6.2 timed out on the SplitMix unit() one-liner `Float(Double(next() >> 11) / Double(1 << 53) * 2 - 1)` in P01OperationsFixtures.swift:133 and P02BatchFixtures.swift:25, and Swift 6.0 on the #expect at D02WitnessDispatchMatrixTests.swift:488. unit() now uses typed steps with 0x1p53 (== Double(1 << 53)); a root harness compared old and new forms over 1,400,004 values (7 seeds x 200,000, plus edge values): 0 bit mismatches. disposition_records.T20-R2-SENDABLE-OPERATOR-REFS: Swift 6.0 rejected 8 bare `+` operator references passed to parallelReduce's `@Sendable` combine (ExecutionSchedulingContractTests 194/198/273/685/686/745, ExecutionBoundaryTests 236/238); Swift 6.2+ infers them Sendable. Each is now `{ $0 + $1 }`, the same operator per site ([Int] concatenation, Int addition, String concatenation). ComputeProvider.parallelReduce's combine was already `@Sendable` on main, so this is test-only and has no consumer impact.
disposition_records.T20-R3-SUMMARY-RENDERING-PARSERS: PR #56 CI run 3 compiled everything on Xcode 16.2 and 26.3; 17/20 checks passed. Both Xcode 16.2 test cells passed every test (1703 Swift Testing, 185 XCTest), then check_performance_gates.py raised 'Representative test did not execute: measured-profile'. XCTest had run the test, and Swift 6.0's Swift Testing runner then printed `Test run with 0 tests passed`, which the gate's `'0 tests passed' in log` check misread; Swift 6.2+ prints `... 0 tests in 0 suites passed`. The class (parsers written against one toolchain's summary rendering) had a second, latent instance: check_sanitizers.verify_body required the 6.2+ `in N suites` rendering. Both now use swiftpm_products.swift_testing_runs / xctest_executed. Mechanical closure: test_test_output_counts pins both renderings, the failing log shape, and a control that keeps the former check; test_sanitizer_log gains Swift 6.0 cases. The independent review swept Scripts/ci for other summary parsers and found none.
